claims.statement: The browser half reaches its host service purely by name over the Connection RPC channel: rpc.call('/api', '<service>/<method>', { args: { request } }), where the service key is the name given to TypertRemoteService at construction ('memo') and the method key is the @Remote wire name, so no generated descriptor or shared runtime object connects the two halves.

Every Remote method must declare exactly one parameter named `request` even when it consumes no input, because the protocol binds arguments by name; a method declared with no parameter was once rejected before its body ran while the host archived 13 quarters successfully, so the read side silently looked like a no-op.

remote-signatures.spec.ts enforces the invariant by scanning the host source for each @Remote('name') and its following signature, asserting the `request` parameter exists, that no second parameter is declared, and — as a guard — that more than ten methods were found and that listArchivedQuarters is among them, so a refactor cannot turn the suite into a silently passing no-op.

The wire carries a double envelope: rpc.call returns a transport envelope { ok, value? , error? } whose value is the method's own business result { ok, value | error }, so the full shape is { ok, value: { ok, value } }; callRemote unwraps only the outer layer and synthesizes 'transport-failure' when the envelope carries no error, 'rpc-failure' when the call throws.

A board click traverses MemoBoard -> MemoController.addCard -> callMemo('memo', 'addEntry', { weekId, type, content }) -> rpc.call with { args: { request } } -> MemoService.addEntry(request) -> private appendEntry -> storage table, and the returned business result is unwrapped from the transport envelope before the board refreshes.

A package that declares dsh.client publishes its browser half at exports['./client'] (lib/client.js), while the package name is itself the boot-graph row id: the host composes the graph from each row's manifest and the browser refuses a bundle that registers under any other id, reporting only 'bundle <url> loaded without registering "<id>"'.

@zhangj1164/dsh-memo is not a dsh.client package: its ./client export is a pure type projection (export type * from './types.ts') that lets browser code consume host request/result types without duplication, so it never becomes a boot row and the preset inlines it as a package with no client half.

clientBundle(id, libEntry, options?) emits three tsdown configs in a fixed order: the node half (ESM, dts, clean true), the browser half (CJS at exactly lib/client.js, clean false, sourcemap on, defines for process.env.NODE_ENV and import.meta.env), and a declarations-only pass, because rolldown emits no declaration chunk for the CJS face wrapped in the module-loader closure.

The browser bundle registers itself through preset-generated output options — banner window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory: (require) => { plus intro/footer that supply module.exports — and the preset resolves its id by locating the workspace package with that manifest name, so a stale id aborts the build before any config is emitted instead of shipping a bundle no boot row can adopt.

A require is answerable only from the module-table word set: PLATFORM_MODULES plus every dsh.client.inject and dsh.client.external row, with <pkg> and <pkg>/client accepted as the same word because the browser normalizes /client before lookup; everything outside that set is inlined by the preset, since a require the table misses throws when the factory materializes.

PLATFORM_MODULES mirrors the DSH shell seed table at 0.2.1-rc.2 (react, react/jsx-runtime, react-dom, react-dom/client, cordis, zod, @tanstack/react-virtual and the four dsh-client-* UI/store packages) and is the single place to update on a shell upgrade: a dropped seed word becomes an unanswerable require while a new shell word missing from the list would be inlined into every bundle.

The dsh-client-bundle-purity plugin turns inlining another plugin's browser half into a build error — because its services, singletons and Remote protocols would exist twice — while type-only imports are erased and never reach the check, which is why no workspace package currently needs a dsh.client.external row.

The preset intentionally carries no CSS pipeline: styles ship as TypeScript string constants, and ui-memo injects its CSS_TEXT once through a <style data-dsh-plugin="memo"> element attached in apply() and removed by the enclosing ctx.effect disposer.

verify-client-bundle-id reads the built artifacts and therefore runs with needs: ['build'] inside gates:check-all; it inspects only packages whose dsh.client.platform is 'web', and reports a missing ./client face or bundle, a missing or mismatched registration id, any literal require outside the answerable words, any non-literal require, and any inject/external row that is not a bare specifier or names a package declaring no dsh.client — with platform-baseline words exempt from that last check because the shell already seeds them.

@Remote is a standard TypeScript decorator, so decorator lowering must be wired into both build paths — ts.transpileModule in the node-half tsdown config, or through the preset's lib override for a package that emits its own Remote service — and the root vitest.config.ts applies the shared standardDecorators() plugin for the test side.

A UI-initiated Remote call happens between turns, where ctx.approval.request() has no open turn to land on, so a capability that needs consent cannot live on this surface: it must stay host-internal with no @Remote registration (as readExternalPath does) or be exposed as a turn-time tool.

scripts/tests/client-bundle-id.spec.ts pins the gate's extraction and row rules — including the shipped regression where the registration id kept the pre-rename name — and scripts/tests/tsdown-client.spec.ts pins the preset's resolution rules, so both ends of the contract have focused tests rather than relying on a booted host.

The single-`request` rule is enforced only for dsh-memo: remote-signatures.spec.ts reads the hardcoded ../src/index.ts, while the same repository ships @zhangj1164/dsh-openwiki-visualize with five parameter-less Remote methods (environment, status, stop, checkUpdate, update) that its browser half still calls as { args: { request: {} } }; host tests call those methods directly and client tests answer through a fake RPC, so no test covers that seam and either the framework tolerates the extra named argument or those five calls never reach the method body.

PLATFORM_MODULES is an eleven-word seed list (react, react/jsx-runtime, react-dom, react-dom/client, cordis, zod, @tanstack/react-virtual and four dsh-client-* UI/store packages) and is not the set of all shell packages: the connection, locale, ui-layout, ui-renderer, ui-theme and ui-settings packages that the three web client halves depend on sit outside the baseline and must therefore be declared in dsh.client.inject to count as answerable rows.

The host service key is hand-duplicated on both sides rather than shared: @zhangj1164/dsh-openwiki-visualize declares the literal 'openwikiVisualize' once in the host half (where it is passed to super()) and once in the browser controller, and alignment is held only by convention plus a client test that asserts the outgoing endpoint is `${SERVICE_KEY}/status`.

One browser half can address two host services through the same /api channel and the same RpcCaller: the memo board calls memo/* through callMemo and githubIssue/optimizeIssue, prefilledIssueUrl and createIssue through callGithubIssue, and its only dependency on the github-issue plugin is the type-only ./client projection of that package.

Both envelope layers land in the same MemoViewState.error string, so a business refusal and a transport failure differ on screen only by wording and by error.code: addCard stores result.error.message and returns false on any unsuccessful result, while readArchivedQuarters folds every failure into an empty quarter set with ok:false and refresh() then raises the fixed warning that the archived quarters could not be read and cards are shown as editable.
